meta.title: Minimal provider-free trust-service prerequisite for bootstrap
meta.author: Terra Tech Lead

feature.problem_statement: Issue #116 needs a minimal trust-service prerequisite linked to #31 bootstrap: a provider-free, workload-bound Ed25519 signing path for preregistration evidence in dev, with durable verifiable evidence and explicit GitOps and security gates. Vault is healthy, but no application role currently exists.
goals: Implement a minimal trust-service inside codicarium/agent-harness for provider-free preregistration signing.
Permit signing only for the approved digest-pinned GitOps Job in trust-service-dev after independently merged canonical preregistration bytes.
Use a non-exportable Vault Transit Ed25519 key, workload-bound identity checks, signed hash-chained evidence, and offline verification.
Deliver only a dev-only Argo application from app-config and enforce internal-only least-privilege access and recoverable durability.
Define artifact, threat-model, focused/full, render/policy, live, and rollback gates before any native GitOps execution.
non_goals: Expose a direct external or local signing endpoint.
Claim WORM storage or physical immutability.
Create a production Argo application or an alternate signing backend.
scope_in: agent-harness implementation slice: src/agent_harness/trust_service/, schemas/prereg.v1.schema.json, golden fixtures/tests, Dockerfile.trust-service, charts/trust-service, image/chart release workflow, and .codicarium/dev/{deploy.yaml,values.yaml}; package only trust-service, never an agent-harness workload.

app-config ad34fbac slice: argocd/apps/dev-config-apps.yaml and generated argocd/self-service-dev-apps/generated/dev-trust-service.yaml using the documented multi-source Helm-OCI values convention and chart charts.nexus.int.codicarium.com/codicarium.

vault-config 6ec510e7 slice: terraform/stacks/vault-vps/{variables.tf,locals.tf,templates/vault-bootstrap.env.tftpl,templates/bootstrap-vault-host.sh} for the non-exportable Transit key/policy and namespace+ServiceAccount JWT role, followed by its controlled bootstrap rollout.
deployment-policy slice: no dev grant; run ./scripts/validate.sh and stop if admission rejects.
TokenReview, pod identity, ServiceAccount, owner Job UID/name, image/status imageID digest, preregistration digest, nonce, expiry, and exact-byte checks.

Internal ClusterIP, least-privilege NetworkPolicy/RBAC, one ceph-rbd-replicated evidence PVC, Retain CSI snapshots, Velero limitation evidence, signed hash-chain export, offline verifier, public-key revision anchor, lifecycle recovery, and rollback evidence.
Issue #116 service-prerequisite linkage to #31 bootstrap, codicarium-local-root app-config evidence, and artifact-before-GitOps gates.
scope_out: Any agent-harness workload deployment or unrelated application deployment.
Any external, local, or unauthenticated signing API.
WORM or physical-immutability guarantees beyond signed tamper evidence, retained snapshots, and export.
Native cluster or GitOps changes before exact slices, destination, policy, durability artifacts, and a fresh merged preregistration are resolved.

requirements.statement: The implementation MUST define trust-service as the minimal service prerequisite for issue #116 and link that prerequisite to the #31 bootstrap scope.
requirements.rationale: The service is a narrowly bounded dependency and must remain traceable to the bootstrap work without expanding application scope.

requirements.statement: app-config MUST supply only a dev-only Argo application for trust-service and MUST NOT deploy an agent-harness workload.
requirements.rationale: Argo ownership and environment scope must be explicit, while the requested service must not be confused with an agent-harness workload deployment.

requirements.statement: The service MUST require a committed codicarium/agent-harness/schemas/prereg.v1.schema.json with additionalProperties:false, an explicit required provider-free fact allowlist, RFC8785/JCS UTF-8 canonical bytes, exact SHA-256 digest matching, golden canonical-byte and digest fixtures, a 256-bit nonce, and expiry. A preregistration PR MUST be independently approved and merged under CODEOWNERS and branch protection before a separate GitOps PR; CI MUST reject absent or mismatched source commit/ref/digest/reviewer proof, and the signer MUST verify the exact submitted bytes.
requirements.rationale: A committed closed schema and byte-level fixtures make preregistration deterministic; independent protected merges and CI provenance prevent a GitOps change from authorizing unreviewed or altered facts.

requirements.statement: Only a digest-pinned GitOps Job running in namespace trust-service-dev MAY request signing; the service MUST reject direct external and local signing requests.
requirements.rationale: The caller boundary is GitOps-controlled workload identity, not a publicly reachable or operator-local endpoint.

requirements.statement: vault-config MUST provision a non-exportable Vault Transit Ed25519 key and a JWT role bound to the trust-service-dev namespace and approved ServiceAccount; it MUST account for the currently absent application role.
requirements.rationale: Vault is healthy, but key use cannot be authorized until the application-specific role and non-exportable signing key exist.

requirements.statement: Before signing, the service MUST require a TokenReview with the expected audience and bound pod UID; GET the Pod and require an exact UID match; require namespace trust-service-dev, the fixed ServiceAccount, and the owning Job UID and name; and require every Job container image and status imageID to equal the exact pinned digest. It MUST reject absent, mismatched, replayed, or external requests and fail closed.
requirements.rationale: Authentication must bind the request to one live pod and its exact immutable Job lineage, not merely to a bearer token or namespace.

requirements.statement: The service MUST require the request preregistration digest to match the independently merged canonical digest and MUST reject nonce reuse or replay.
requirements.rationale: Digest binding protects the input and nonce replay defense prevents reusing an otherwise valid authorization.

requirements.statement: Accepted operations MUST produce a single-writer, fsynced, signed hash-chained evidence record with deterministic linkage to the prior record and no silent truncation or rewrite.
requirements.rationale: The audit trail must expose tampering and preserve a durable order of signing decisions.

requirements.statement: Evidence MUST be exportable and verifiable offline with the public key and an explicit Vault key revision anchor.
requirements.rationale: Independent verification must remain possible without access to the service, Vault, or a live cluster.

requirements.statement: The service MUST be reachable only through an internal Kubernetes ClusterIP and MUST expose no direct external or local signing endpoint.
requirements.rationale: Network reachability must enforce the workload-bound trust boundary.

requirements.statement: Kubernetes RBAC and NetworkPolicy MUST grant only the minimum permissions required for TokenReview, the approved workload path, Vault authentication, evidence persistence, and observability.
requirements.rationale: Least privilege limits blast radius if the service, Job, or a neighboring workload is compromised.

requirements.statement: The service MUST use exactly one ceph-rbd-replicated evidence PVC with Delete reclaim for the primary PVC only. A namespaced six-hour snapshot CronJob MUST use VolumeSnapshotClass csi-rbdplugin-snapclass with Retain and minimal VolumeSnapshot RBAC. The current Velero dev-cluster-resources schedule (17 */6 * * *, TTL 168h) has PVC snapshots false and MUST NOT be claimed as protection. Claims are limited to signed hash-chain tamper evidence plus retained snapshots and export, never WORM or physical immutability.
requirements.rationale: The specified PVC and retained CSI snapshots support recovery while accurately acknowledging that the current Velero schedule does not snapshot PVCs and that neither mechanism is WORM.

requirements.statement: Key provisioning, rotation, revocation, and recovery MUST preserve the public-key revision anchor, fail closed on revoked or unavailable revisions, and document evidence recovery without exporting private key material.
requirements.rationale: Key lifecycle events must not invalidate historical verification or permit signing during an unsafe transition.

requirements.statement: The threat boundary MUST name assets (Transit key/sign authority, preregistration, chain/PVC/snapshots, and public anchor), attackers (local runner, replaying caller, compromised namespace pod, GitOps author, and cluster/Vault/backup admin), and concrete mitigations: closed schema and exact JCS/SHA-256 bytes, 256-bit nonce/expiry, protected independent prereg merge, CI commit/ref/digest/reviewer proof, TokenReview audience and pod UID plus Pod GET/owner/imageID checks, fixed namespace/ServiceAccount/Job, ClusterIP/NetworkPolicy/RBAC, non-exportable Transit key, fsynced signed chain, retained snapshots/export, offline revision anchor, and tested lifecycle recovery. The residual boundary MUST state that admin deletion or key misuse is detectable and recoverable only; evidence is never WORM or physically immutable. Artifact-before-GitOps gates MUST require those threat/key artifacts, all exact implementation paths, adversarial and focused/full tests, render/policy checks, explicit destination preflight, live positive and negative proof, a fresh merged preregistration, and rollback proof before native execution.
requirements.rationale: Explicit assets, attacker capabilities, mitigations, and residual limits make the high-risk trust boundary reviewable and prevent durability or administrator-resistance claims that the design cannot support.

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Given issue #116 is recorded as the service prerequisite linked to #31 bootstrap, when app-config ownership is reviewed, then codicarium-local-root in argocd has namespace creation true and the default project, trust-service-dev is absent or precreated only by the child Application, the two app-config paths are the owned slices, and no agent-harness workload deployment is introduced.

Given schemas/prereg.v1.schema.json is committed with additionalProperties:false, provider-free required-fact allowlist, RFC8785/JCS UTF-8 bytes, SHA-256, golden bytes/digest fixtures, 256-bit nonce, and expiry, when CODEOWNERS/branch protection independently approves and merges the prereg PR before a separate GitOps PR, then CI proves source commit/ref/digest/reviewer agreement and only the exact digest-pinned trust-service-dev Job is eligible; the signer still verifies exact bytes and rejects external or local requests.

Given Vault is healthy but has no application role, when the controlled vault-config 6ec510e7 bootstrap rollout is applied and lifecycle procedures are exercised, then a non-exportable Transit Ed25519 key/policy and namespace/ServiceAccount-bound JWT role are provisioned, rotated, revocable, recoverable, and never export private key material.

Given a request has a TokenReview with expected audience and bound pod UID, an exact GET Pod UID, namespace trust-service-dev, fixed ServiceAccount, owning Job UID/name, every Job image and status imageID at the pinned digest, preregistration digest, 256-bit nonce, and expiry, when any field is absent, mismatched, replayed, or external, then the service fails closed and emits no signing evidence.

Given an authorized signing operation succeeds, when its evidence is exported and checked without the service or cluster, then the signed hash chain and public-key revision anchor verify offline and tampering, reordering, or an invalid signature fails verification.

Given the rendered dev deployment is inspected, when network, RBAC, storage, snapshot, and backup policies are evaluated, then one ceph-rbd-replicated evidence PVC uses Delete for the primary only, a namespaced six-hour snapshot CronJob uses csi-rbdplugin-snapclass Retain with minimal VolumeSnapshot RBAC, current Velero dev-cluster-resources (17 */6 * * *, TTL 168h, PVC snapshots false) is not claimed as protection, access is internal ClusterIP and least privilege, and no WORM or physical-immutability claim exists.

Given all exact source, chart, config, deployment-policy, threat-model, and key-lifecycle artifacts are independently merged and a fresh preregistration merge is present, when adversarial, focused/full, render, policy, explicit live positive/negative destination, and rollback checks complete, then the artifact-before-GitOps gate passes or native execution remains blocked.

test_plan.approach: Review the threat boundary assets/attackers/mitigations/residuals, issue linkage, exact artifact ownership, Vault key provisioning/rotation/revocation/recovery runbook, Retain and Velero limitation evidence, and artifact-before-GitOps checklist; no native command may run before deployment artifacts and a fresh merged preregistration exist.

Run `uv run ruff format --check .`, `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run mypy src`, `uv run pytest`, and the focused adversarial suite under tests/trust_service/ for provider-free prereg.v1 bytes, additionalProperties:false schema, RFC8785/JCS UTF-8, SHA-256, golden fixtures, 256-bit nonce/expiry, TokenReview identity/owner/image checks, replay, fail-closed authorization, signed chaining, revision anchors, and offline verification.

Run `uv run pytest tests/trust_service/` for focused and full service integration coverage with Vault Transit and Kubernetes identity fixtures; require positive approved digest-pinned Job signing, negative absent/mismatched/replayed/external callers, key revisions, durable evidence writes, export, and offline verification.

Run `uv run python scripts/generate_schemas.py --check`, `helm template trust-service charts/trust-service --namespace trust-service-dev --values .codicarium/dev/values.yaml`, and the exact deployment-policy `./scripts/validate.sh`; reject render/policy output for wrong Argo destination, any agent-harness workload, external Service, excess RBAC/NetworkPolicy, mutable image, or missing gate.

After explicit `kubectl --context <DEV_CONTEXT>` and `argocd --server <ARGO_SERVER> app get <APP> --project <ARGO_PROJECT>` preflight, and only after deployment plus a fresh merged preregistration, run dev-only positive approved signing and negative absent/mismatched/replayed/external requests, evidence export, snapshot/Velero recovery, key revocation, and GitOps rollback; record exact target identity and stop on mismatch or deployment-policy admission rejection.

review_checks: Confirm issue #116 service prerequisite is explicitly linked to #31 bootstrap and scope remains minimal.
validation_checks: Verify the resolved source and app-config ownership artifacts before implementation.

review_checks: Inspect app-config for a dev-only Argo application and absence of an agent-harness workload deployment.
validation_checks: Render and explicitly inspect Argo destination, namespace, and workload ownership.

review_checks: Review prereg.v1 field contract, provider-free canonical bytes, JCS serialization, and independent digest merge gate.
validation_checks: Run canonicalization and digest mismatch tests with exact byte fixtures.

review_checks: Confirm only the digest-pinned trust-service-dev GitOps Job is an eligible signer caller.
validation_checks: Exercise direct external and local request rejection and approved Job acceptance.

review_checks: Review Vault Transit Ed25519 non-exportability and namespace/ServiceAccount-bound JWT role provisioning.
validation_checks: Verify Vault role and key artifacts exist before any GitOps authorization.

review_checks: Check fail-closed TokenReview, pod, namespace, ServiceAccount, owner, and image-digest binding.
validation_checks: Run adversarial identity substitution and stale image-digest fixtures.

review_checks: Review exact preregistration digest comparison and nonce lifecycle/replay policy.
validation_checks: Run wrong-digest, modified-bytes, duplicate-nonce, and replay rejection tests.

review_checks: Inspect single-writer ordering, fsync boundary, signed record, and hash-chain linkage.
validation_checks: Test tamper, reorder, truncation, restart, and concurrent-write behavior.

review_checks: Confirm exported evidence carries public key and immutable Vault key revision anchor for offline use.
validation_checks: Run the offline verifier against valid and tampered exported evidence.

review_checks: Inspect Service and ingress policy for internal ClusterIP only and no direct signing endpoint.
validation_checks: Render and live-check reachability from approved and unapproved network identities.

review_checks: Review minimum RBAC verbs/resources and deny-by-default NetworkPolicy paths.
validation_checks: Run render/policy enforcement and permission-negative checks.

review_checks: Confirm snapshot Retain and Velero six-hour cadence/168-hour retention without WORM language.
validation_checks: Verify backup/restore evidence and accurately report residual durability limits.

review_checks: Review key rotation, revocation, recovery, revision anchoring, and private-material handling.
validation_checks: Perform live or controlled lifecycle rollback checks and prove revoked revisions cannot sign.

review_checks: Confirm every source, chart, config, policy, threat-model, and key artifact is independently merged before GitOps.
validation_checks: Require adversarial, focused/full, render, policy, explicit live-target, and rollback validation evidence.

perspectives.summary: Pass: exact provider-free canonical bytes, Ed25519 Transit non-exportability, TokenReview identity binding, nonce replay defense, least privilege, and explicit non-WORM residual risk are specified.
Pass: single-writer fsynced signed hash chain, Retain snapshots, Velero six-hour cadence, 168-hour retention, recovery, and offline evidence verification are specified.
Pass: dev-only app-config ownership, digest-pinned Job, internal destination, artifact-before-GitOps gates, and no agent-harness workload deployment are explicit.
Pass: threat model, adversarial/focused/full, render/policy, live destination, key lifecycle, evidence, and rollback checks are measurable prerequisites.

council.consensus_summary: Implementation-ready for planning only; native execution remains unauthorized until source/chart ownership, deployment policy, exact dev destination, Retain class, key provisioning, and Velero restore artifacts are resolved.
open_questions: Resolve exact source repository and chart path for codicarium/agent-harness trust-service.
Resolve deployment-policy repository/path and approved DeploymentProfile/DeploymentGrant.
Resolve explicit dev context, Argo server/project/application/destination, and trust-service-dev namespace ownership.
Resolve Retain StorageClass, Vault key provisioning artifact, and Velero backup/restore artifact.
